creator: ai.honeycove
title: Five front-end plugins for Claude Code: taste-skill, Vercel web design guidelines skill (audits code against Vercel's rules), Awesome DESIGN.md, image-to-code, and Playwright CLI for self-screenshotting

tools.name: taste-skill
tools.detail: Pulls design taste from premium references

tools.name: Vercel web design guidelines skill
tools.detail: Audits code against Vercel's latest design rules; on-screen excerpt: 'Keyboard works everywhere... Clear focus (focus-visible)... Match visual & hit targets (min 24px, 44px mobile)... Mobile input size 16px to prevent iOS auto-zoom... Respect zoom... Hydration-safe inputs... Don't block paste... Loading buttons... Minimum loading-state duration (150-300ms delay, 300-500ms visible)... URL as state'

tools.name: Awesome DESIGN.md
tools.detail: 'Curated collection of DESIGN.md analysis by developer focused websites'; DESIGN.md is a Google Stitch concept: plain-text design system file read by agents; table AGENTS.md (how to build) vs DESIGN.md (look and feel)

tools.name: image-to-code
tools.detail: Turns a design reference image into usable code

tools.name: Playwright CLI
tools.detail: Lets Claude open a browser, screenshot what it built and catch errors

claims: taste-skill stops UI looking 'crappy and vibe coded'
The Vercel guideline skill flags weak points before you ship
Awesome DESIGN.md hands the AI a full design system (colors, typography, spacing, buttons) pulled from top websites
image-to-code converts any reference to code without losing details
Playwright CLI lets Claude screenshot its own output and catch bad outputs/errors before you see them
how_to_steps: Install Vercel's web design guidelines skill and run its audit before shipping
Copy a DESIGN.md from Awesome DESIGN.md into the project root and tell the agent to build to it
Use image-to-code with a reference screenshot
Install Playwright CLI so Claude can open, screenshot and verify pages
on_screen_only: Title '5 claude code PLUGINS TO INSTALL'

Vercel web design rules list: 'Interfaces succeed because of hundreds of choices... framework-agnostic, some specific to React/Next.js'; items: Keyboard works everywhere (WAI-ARIA Authoring Patterns), Clear focus (prefer :focus-visible), Manage focus (focus traps, move & return focus), Match visual & hit targets (<24px visual -> expand hit area to 24px; 44px on mobile), Mobile input size (16px font to prevent iOS Safari zoom; viewport meta maximum-scale=1), Respect zoom (never disable browser zoom), Hydration-safe inputs, Don't block paste, Loading buttons (show indicator, keep original label), Minimum loading-state duration (150-300ms show-delay, 300-500ms min visible; Suspense in React does this), URL as state

Awesome DESIGN.md README: 'Copy a DESIGN.md into your project, tell your AI agent build me a page that looks like this'; 'DESIGN.md is a new concept introduced by Google Stitch'; table File / Who reads it / What it defines: AGENTS.md - Coding agents - How to build the project; DESIGN.md - Design agents - look and feel

Design reference panels: Colors, Typography (Heading/Subheading), Spacing bars, Buttons (Get Started / Learn more); a 'CHECKOUT' page in a Playwright terminal with a warning about 'priority' prop on a non-LCP image

relevance.why: Three of five (taste-skill, awesome-design, Playwright) are already in the liked set; the Vercel web-design-guidelines audit skill is a concrete accessibility/UX checklist (hit targets, iOS zoom, loading states) that matters for Haji's shipped apps.

implement_score.why: Add the Vercel web design guidelines skill and run it as a pre-ship audit on existing apps (~30 min); the rules shown (44px mobile targets, 16px inputs, focus-visible, loading-state minimums) are worth adopting even without the skill.

verify: Vercel web design guidelines skill: exact repo (likely under vercel-labs) and whether it is a skill or just a doc
Awesome DESIGN.md: repo name and whether its DESIGN.md files are extracted from sites with usable licenses

gap.what: Adds Vercel's web-design-guidelines audit skill (with specific rules: 24/44px hit targets, 16px mobile inputs, focus-visible, 150-300ms loading delay, URL as state) and an image-to-code skill; the other three are duplicates of liked content.
